sentences.text:
Brief facts of Petitioner's case, are as under:
On 02-08-2022 at about 09-15 p.m, while the petitioner was boarding the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-2899 in Singaiahnapalya Bus Stop, Bangalore City, at that time driver of said bus moved the same without closing the door.

As a result of which,
the Petitioner had lost control over the same and fell down and rear wheel of the said bus ran over his left leg and sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Vydehi Hospital for first aid, then he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery and was forced to spend more than Rs.2,00,000/-
3 SCCH - 19 MVC.5208/2022 towards medical expenses conveyance, food, transport and other charges.
4.

It is contended that, this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, hence, the K.R.Puram Traffic Police had registered a case against driver of offending vehicle crime No.124/2022.
5.
It is contended that, prior to the date of accident, the petitioner was hale, healthy and he was doing Coolie and earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day.
Due to injuries he is not able to do his work as before the accident and hence lost his earnings and suffering from mental shock, pain and agony.
Hence, prayed to grant compensation.
6. In pursuance to the notice, Respondent appeared through it's Counsel & filed written statement.

7. Brief averments of the written statement of Respondent as under:
The petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

While admitting 4 SCCH - 19 MVC.5208/2022 about ownership of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-2899 this Respondent took specific contention that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the Petitioner himself.
It is contended that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of bus and hence there is a delay in lodging the complaint.

Further, denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and contending that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.

8. On basis of the Pleadings and materials, this tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 02-08- Sri.Murthy .R. S/O Rathnam vs The Managing Director on 11 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47480389/
2 2022 at about 09-15 p.m, while he was boarding the bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-2899 at Singaiahnapalya Bus Stop, Bangalore City, at that time driver of said bus, moved the same without closed the door.
As a result of which, the Petitioner lost control over the same and fell down and rear wheel of the said bus ran over his left leg and sustained grievous injuries?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
5 SCCH - 19 MVC.5208/2022 3. Whether order or award?
9. In order to substantiate the case, Petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got one witness as Pw.2.
They got marked 14 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
On the other hand, driver of the offending vehicle got examined as RW.1 and had not got marked any document.

10. Heard the arguments of both side and Perused the materials available on hand.
11.

For the following reasons, I answer the above Issues as under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
REASONS 12. Issue No.1:-
The Petitioner filed this petition against respondents, for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The Petitioner Sri.Murthy .R. got examined himself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and in his Chief affidavit he had reiterated the contention of petition and got marked 12 documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.

Ex.P1 is the Certified Copy of F.I.R. Ex.P2 is the Certified Copy of Complaint, Ex.P3 is the Certified Copy of Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4 is the Certified Copy of Spot sketch,
Ex.P5 is the Certified Copy of IMV report, Ex.P6 is the Certified Copy of wound certificate, Ex.P7 is the Certified Copy of Charge sheet, Ex.P8 is the Certified Copy of Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act,
Ex.P9 is the Certified Copy of reply to the Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P10 is the discharge summary, Ex.P11 is the Medical bills and Ex.P12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhaar card.
14. Sri
.Nagaraj B.N. the Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS examined as PW.2 and got marked two documents as Ex.P13 and 14.
Ex.P13 is the Clinical examination report and Ex.P14 is the X-ray.

sentences.text: The driver of offending vehicle Sri.T.K.Devaraja got examined himself as RW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and in his affidavit he had reiterated the contention of Written statement.
In the Cross examination Rw.1 deposed that, " It is true to suggest that, said bus had automatic door and driver was having control over the door.
It is true to suggest that once the passengers get into the bus, then only bus will move."

16. On perusal of the spot sketch & Charge sheet it disclose that near Singaiahnapalya the driver of offending vehicle moved his bus in a rash and negligent manner, while the Petitioner was boarding the bus, as a result, the Petitioner lost his control and fell down and sustained injuries.

Hence, the K.R.Puram Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-2899 in crime No.124/2022.
8 SCCH - 19 MVC.5208/2022 17.

In the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the claimant has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble APEX Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others.

entities.text: 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The so-called reason that as the name of Dheeraj Kumar was not mentioned in the FIR, so it was not possible for Dheeraj Kumar to see the incident, is not a proper assessment of the fact-situation in this case.
It is well known that in a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Court must keep this distinction in mind.

10. Reference in this connection may be made to the decision of this Court in Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, in which the relevant observation on this point has been made and which is very pertinent and is quoted below:-
"In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."

After careful scrutiny of Ex.P1-FIR, Ex.P2- Complaint, Ex.P3-Spot Mahazar, Ex.P4 Spot sketch,
Ex.P5 IMV report, Ex.P6-Wound Certificate and Ex.P7 Charge sheet it appears that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-2899.
Accordingly I answer Issue no.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
The Petitioner had claimed the compensation amount of Rs.20,00,000/- with respect to road traffic accident.

As per Ex.P6 Wound certificate the petitioner sustained following injuries:
1) Abrasion present over left thigh 2) laceration present over left posterior aspect of leg.
The doctor opined that the above said injuries are grievous in nature.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injuries, I am of the opinion that, Petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.80,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.

The Petitioner produced the Medical bills and Hospital bills, which are marked as Ex.P11.
Sl.No.1, 6 and 16 are one and the same, hence, one bill is taken into consideration.
Sl.No.13 is advance receipt, hence, said bill is not considered.
There is no any contradictions to disbelieve the other medical bills produced by the Petitioner.

Hence, considering the medical bills and also treatment taken by the Petitioner in the hospital, the Petitioner is entitled to claim the medical bill amount of Rs.5,851/- under the head of medical expenditure.

21. The Petitioner had produced two discharge summaries issued by Victoria hospital as per Ex.P10 which disclose that the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the said hospital:
a) from 03-08-2022 to 05-08-2022 & b) from 05-08-2022 to 26-08-2022 for 24 days.
Therefore, considering the treatment taken as inpatient in the hospital this tribunal has awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.25,000/- under the head Transportation, Nourishment and conveyance charges.
11 SCCH - 19 MVC.5208/2022 22.
To prove the assessment of disability, the Petitioner got examined the Doctor Shri.B.N.Nagaraj as PW-2.

In the affidavit doctor deposed that, on 04-02-2023 the Petitioner went to him for assessment of disability and also deposed that, on examination the Petitioner has unhealthy scar over the left thigh with wasting of left thigh muscles and restricted left knee movements.
Recent X-ray of left thigh shows no bony injuries.
Further assessed total physical disability of left lower limb at 33% and that of to the whole body at 11%.
In the cross examination deposed that, "I am not a treated doctor.
I examined the Petitioner after 8 months from the date of accident.
It is true to suggest that, the Petitioner is fully recovered and Petitioner was stable when he was discharged."
However by considering the nature of the wound and evidence of the doctor this Tribunal has taken the disability of the Petitioner at 9% to the whole body.

sentences.text: The Petitioner contended that, at the time of accident he was Coolie by Profession and and earning a sum of Rs.1,000/- per day and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to carry on his duty as earlier.
The Petitioner had not produced any document to prove his actual income and avocation.
In present days the coolie worker get Rs.400/- to 500/- per day.

Therefore by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal has taken notional income of Rs.15,000/- p.m.
24.
As per Ex.P12 notarized copy of Aadhaar card date of birth-year of the Petitioner is shown as 1964.
As per Ex.P6 wound certificate the age of the Petitioner is mentioned as 58 years.

Therefore,
age of the Petitioner is considered as 58 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 09 which comes as follows:
Rs.15,000 x 12 x 9 x 9% = Rs.1,45,800/-
Hence, this tribunal awarded Rs.1,45,800/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
13 SCCH - 19 MVC.5208/2022 25.
The Petitioner sustained grievous injury and took as treatment as inpatient for 24 days in the hospital.
The Petitioner is a Coolie by Profession and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

Therefore, by considering this aspect and the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, this tribunal awarded the amount of Rs.30,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of loss of amenities.

26. Considering oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:

4. Towards loss of future income Rs. 1,45,800-00
due to permanent disability 5. Towards loss of amenities of Rs. 30,000-00  life  Total Rs. 2,86,651-00

6
The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,86,651/-.
It is rounded off to Rs.2,86,700/-.
Interest:

For awarding interest, in MFA.No.103557/2016 (between Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others, dd 20-03-2018) the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, held that as per Sec.34 of CPC the rate of interest can be awarded in MVC Cases, cannot be more than 6% p.a.
Hence, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for interest @6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of payment.
28. Liability:-
As per the petition, Respondent is the Owner -cum- Insurer of the offending vehicle i.e., BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-2899.

entities.text: Sriram General Insurance Co. ltd., V/s Smt. Lakshmi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As already discussed in the issue no.1 it is proved that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the Respondent is held liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer the Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

29. Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
15 SCCH - 19 MVC.5208/2022 ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,86,700/- (rupees Two lakhs, Eighty six thousand and Seven hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further, Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this Order.

After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner (as the Petitioner is Coolie by profession and he is aged person) with proper verification and identification of the documents.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.

The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.2,86,700/- (rupees Two lakhs, Eighty six thousand and Seven hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Further, Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation together with 6% interest within 60 days, from the date of this Order.

After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner (as the Petitioner is Coolie by profession and he is aged person) with proper verification and identification of the documents.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
